SecWatch Notes · independent security research blog · 18 March 2026

Kestrel Ridge Analytics confirms exposure of retail customer data

Customer-analytics vendor Kestrel Ridge Analytics has confirmed that a misconfigured cloud storage bucket exposed data belonging to several of its retail clients between January and early March 2026.

According to the company's notice to customers, the bucket held loyalty-programme exports containing names, email addresses and phone numbers for roughly 1.2 million end customers. Kestrel Ridge says it found no evidence that payment data was involved.

The exposure was reported to the company by an independent researcher on 2 February 2026. Affected clients were notified on 14 March, about six weeks later. Kestrel Ridge says it has since locked down the bucket, rotated keys and engaged an external firm to review its cloud configuration, and that the review is ongoing.

Questions remain about why the bucket was public for several weeks and whether the delay in notifying clients met contractual timelines.

SecWatch Notes and Kestrel Ridge Analytics are fictional, created for a security demonstration.
